question: The Commission is due to publish two executive acts before 8 July enabling European tuna seiner, small pelagic and industrial fleets to apply a 10% margin of tolerance on total catches in some ports, provided the necessary weighing and control equipment is available. These acts must provide for equal access to this exemption, whether in Europe or in third countries, including developing ones. 1.

Given that the Commission stated at an inter-council advisory meeting its intention to enforce stricter criteria than those in the control regulation itself for using this exemption, are the planned criteria realistic and enforceable, particularly in developing countries?
Will these criteria ensure equal treatment not only of European and other fleets – including Asian ones – in third countries, but also among European fleets themselves?
Will it fall to Member States to monitor compliance, since only they have the authority to enforce the control regulation in third countries?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (26.6.2024) As prescribed by Article 14(4) of the Regulation (EC) 1224/20091 (‘the Control Regulation’) revised by Regulation (EU) 2023/28422, the Commission adopted on 24 May 2024 an implementing act3 that lays down the conditions and safeguards for the use of certain margin of tolerance (MOT) derogations.
Following Member States’ applications, a subsequent implementing act will list the ports, in and outside the EU, that comply with such conditions.

All vessels authorised to fish in Union waters landing or transhipping in listed Union ports, or EU vessels landing and transhipping in listed ports outside the EU, would be able to claim the derogation to the MOT for the species concerned by the derogation in those ports and provided the specific conditions listed in the implementing act are fulfilled.

The implementation of the derogation and the associated conditions have been conceived in such a way that weighing and reporting of the catches generate reliable data. To do so, the Commission designed the conditions in cooperation with Member States and stakeholders, taking into consideration the operational model of the concerned EU fishing vessels within and outside Union ports.

The result is a set of conditions that apply to ports in and outside the EU and additional conditions relating to the landing, transhipment and weighing of catches of fisheries covered by the derogation and ensuring equal treatment for all concerned fleets.

Member States have to enforce and monitor compliance with the Control Regulation of the vessels flying their flag in and outside Union waters and take necessary action in the event of non-compliance. The implementing act includes the obligation for Member States to conduct inspections and annual reporting to the Commission.
1 Council Regulation (EC) No 1224/2009 of 20 November 2009 establishing a Community control system for
